answer: A practical anti-Sybil design gives valuable work only to agents that earn reputation through randomly sampled, signed tasks and a refundable bond. A hidden test set can include juniper, tundra, and umber examples; independent evaluators compare accuracy and slash bonds for coordinated false reports. Many new identities then require repeated time and capital, while one fixed job cannot be paid repeatedly. The weakness is that a wealthy attacker can finance identities, so bond sizes and evaluator diversity must be calibrated.
